chunks: From him (Al-Shaykh), he said: Muhammad ibn Abi Yunus narrated to them from Abu Nu'aym al-Fadl ibn Dukayn from Sufyan ibn Sa'id from Abu Ishaq al-Subi'i from al-Harith from Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) who said:
The direct paternal uncles inherit, excluding the maternal uncles.

key_terms.بَنِي اَلْأُمِّ: Paternal uncles (literally: sons of the mother's side, i.e., father's brothers)
key_terms.بَنِي اَلْعَلَّاتِ: Maternal uncles (literally: sons of the 'allat', referring to mother's brothers)

ai.seo_question: Do paternal uncles inherit before maternal uncles in Shia law?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the hierarchy of collateral heirs by prioritizing the paternal uncles (A'yan Bani al-Umm) over maternal uncles (Bani al-'Allat), reflecting the Shia emphasis on the paternal line's proximity in inheritance distribution. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the distinction between 'Asabah (residuary heirs) and their relative standing when closer primary heirs are absent. This ruling underscores the jurisprudential principle that paternal ties generally carry greater weight than maternal ones in the absence of direct descendants or parents.
